View.name: View
View.doc: Superclass for all the other views Lifecycle of a view is :  new -> [willAppear -> willDisappear] -> delete Users have do to the new, the rest of the lifecycle is taken care of by the library willAppear and willDisappear can be called zero or multiple times before deletion (in case of a TabLayout for instance)

methods.name: invalidate
methods.doc: Triggers a layout of the whole view tree. Must be called after a yoga node property is changed. Only methods that change yoga nodes properties should call this method.

methods.name: onLayout
methods.doc: Called when a layout pass ends on that view.

methods.name: getView
methods.doc: Returns the view with the corresponding id in the view or its children, or nullptr if it hasn't been found. Research is done recursively by traversing the tree starting from this view. This view's parents are not traversed.

methods.name: setWidth
methods.doc: Sets the preferred width of the view. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically resize the view. If set to anything else than AUTO, the view is guaranteed to never shrink below the given width.

methods.name: setHeight
methods.doc: Sets the preferred height of the view. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically resize the view. If set to anything else than AUTO, the view is guaranteed to never shrink below the given height.

methods.name: setSize
methods.doc: Sets the preferred width and height of the view. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically resize the view. If set to anything else than AUTO, the view is guaranteed to never shrink below the given height.

methods.name: setDimensions
methods.doc: Shortcut to setWidth + setHeight. Only does one layout pass instead of two when using the two methods separately.

methods.name: setWidthPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the preferred width of the view in percentage of the parent view width. Between 0.0f and 100.0f.

methods.name: setHeightPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the preferred height of the view in percentage of the parent view height. Between 0.0f and 100.0f.

methods.name: setMinWidth
methods.doc: Sets the minimum width of the view, in pixels. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be less than the given min width. Use View::AUTO to disable the min width constraint.

methods.name: setMinHeight
methods.doc: Sets the minimum height of the view, in pixels. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be less than the given max height. Use View::AUTO to disable the min height constraint.

methods.name: setMinWidthPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the minimum width of the view, in parent width percentage. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be less than the given max width. Use View::AUTO to disable the min width constraint.

methods.name: setMinHeightPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the minimum height of the view, in parent height percentage. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be less than the given max height. Use View::AUTO to disable the min height constraint.

methods.name: setMaxWidth
methods.doc: Sets the maximum width of the view, in pixels. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be larger than the given max width. Use View::AUTO to disable the max width constraint.

methods.name: setMaxHeight
methods.doc: Sets the maximum height of the view, in pixels. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be larger than the given max height. Use View::AUTO to disable the max height constraint.

methods.name: setMaxWidthPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the maximum width of the view, in parent width percentage. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be larger than the given max width. Use View::AUTO to disable the max width constraint.

methods.name: setMaxHeightPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the maximum height of the view, in parent height percentage. This constraint is stronger than the grow factor: the view is guaranteed to never be larger than the given max height. Use View::AUTO to disable the max height constraint.

methods.name: setGrow
methods.doc: Sets the grow factor of the view, aka the percentage of remaining space to give this view, in the containing box axis. Opposite of shrink. Default is 0.0f;

methods.name: setShrink
methods.doc: Sets the shrink factor of the view, aka the percentage of space the view is allowed to shrink for if there is not enough space for everyone in the contaning box axis. Opposite of grow. Default is 1.0f;

methods.sig: void setMargins(float top, float right, float bottom, float left)
methods.name: setMargins
methods.doc: Sets the margin of the view, aka the space that separates this view and the surrounding ones in all 4 directions. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically select the margin. Only works with views that have parents - top level views that are pushed on the stack don't have parents. Only does one layout pass instead of four when using the four methods separately.

methods.name: setMarginTop
methods.doc: Sets the top margin of the view, aka the space that separates this view and the surrounding ones. Only works with views that have parents - top level views that are pushed on the stack don't have parents. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically select the margin.

methods.name: setMarginRight
methods.doc: Sets the right margin of the view, aka the space that separates this view and the surrounding ones. Only works with views that have parents - top level views that are pushed on the stack don't have parents. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically select the margin.

methods.name: setMarginBottom
methods.doc: Sets the bottom margin of the view, aka the space that separates this view and the surrounding ones. Only works with views that have parents - top level views that are pushed on the stack don't have parents. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically select the margin.

methods.name: setMarginLeft
methods.doc: Sets the right margin of the view, aka the space that separates this view and the surrounding ones. Only works with views that have parents - top level views that are pushed on the stack don't have parents. Use brls::View::AUTO to have the layout automatically select the margin.

methods.name: setVisibility
methods.doc: Sets the visibility of the view.

methods.name: getVisibility
methods.doc: Gets the visibility of the view.

methods.name: setPositionTop
methods.doc: Sets the top position of the view, in pixels. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view. If relative, it will simply offset the view by the given amount. If absolute, it will behave like the "display: absolute;" CSS property and move the view freely in its parent. Use 0 to snap to the parent top edge. Absolute positioning ignores padding. Use View::AUTO to disable (not the same as 0).

methods.name: setPositionRight
methods.doc: Sets the right position of the view, in pixels. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view. If relative, it will simply offset the view by the given amount. If absolute, it will behave like the "display: absolute;" CSS property and move the view freely in its parent. Use 0 to snap to the parent right edge. Absolute positioning ignores padding. Use View::AUTO to disable (not the same as 0).

methods.name: setPositionBottom
methods.doc: Sets the bottom position of the view, in pixels. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view. If relative, it will simply offset the view by the given amount. If absolute, it will behave like the "display: absolute;" CSS property and move the view freely in its parent. Use 0 to snap to the parent bottom edge. Absolute positioning ignores padding. Use View::AUTO to disable (not the same as 0).

methods.name: setPositionLeft
methods.doc: Sets the left position of the view, in pixels. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view. If relative, it will simply offset the view by the given amount. If absolute, it will behave like the "display: absolute;" CSS property and move the view freely in its parent. Use 0 to snap to the parent left edge. Absolute positioning ignores padding. Use View::AUTO to disable (not the same as 0).

methods.name: setPositionTopPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the top position of the view, in percents. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view.

methods.name: setPositionRightPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the right position of the view, in percents. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view.

methods.name: setPositionBottomPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the bottom position of the view, in percentage. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view.

methods.name: setPositionLeftPercentage
methods.doc: Sets the left position of the view, in percents. The behavior of this attribute changes depending on the position type of the view.

methods.name: setPositionType
methods.doc: Sets the "position type" of the view, aka the behavior of the 4 position attributes. Default is RELATIVE.

methods.name: setId
methods.doc: Sets the id of the view.

methods.name: setAlignSelf
methods.doc: Overrides align items of the parent box. Default is AUTO.

methods.name: setLineColor
methods.doc: Sets the line color for the view. To be used with setLineTop(), setLineRight()... The "line" is separate from the shape "border".

methods.name: setLineTop
methods.doc: Sets the top line thickness. Use setLineColor() to change the line color. The "line" is separate from the shape "border".

methods.name: setLineRight
methods.doc: Sets the right line thickness. Use setLineColor() to change the line color. The "line" is separate from the shape "border".

methods.name: setLineBottom
methods.doc: Sets the bottom line thickness. Use setLineColor() to change the line color. The "line" is separate from the shape "border".

methods.name: setLineLeft
methods.doc: Sets the left line thickness. Use setLineColor() to change the line color. The "line" is separate from the shape "border".

methods.name: setBackgroundColor
methods.doc: Sets the view shape background color.

methods.name: setBorderColor
methods.doc: Sets the view shape border color.

methods.name: setBorderThickness
methods.doc: Sets the view shape border thickness.

methods.name: setCornerRadius
methods.doc: Sets the view shape corner radius. 0 means no rounded corners.

methods.name: setShadowType
methods.doc: Sets the view shape shadow type. Default is NONE.

methods.name: setShadowVisibility
methods.doc: Sets the shadow visibility.

methods.name: setHideHighlightBackground
methods.doc: If set to true, the highlight background will be hidden for this view (the white rectangle that goes behind the view, replacing the usual background shape).

methods.name: setHideHighlightBorder
methods.doc: If set to true, the highlight border will be hidden for this view.

methods.name: setHideHighlight
methods.doc: If set to true, the highlight will be hidden for this view.

methods.name: setHighlightPadding
methods.doc: Sets the highlight padding of the view, aka the space between the highlight rectangle and the view. The highlight rect is enlarged, the view is untouched.

methods.name: setHighlightCornerRadius
methods.doc: Sets the highlight rectangle corner radius.

methods.name: getNearestView
methods.doc: Returns the "nearest" view with the corresponding id, or nullptr if none has been found. "Nearest" means the closest in the vicinity of this view. The siblings are searched as well as its children. Research is done by traversing the tree upwards, starting from this view. The current algorithm is very inefficient.

methods.name: createFromXMLString
methods.doc: Creates a view from the given XML file content. The method handleXMLElement() is executed for each child node in the XML. Uses the internal lookup table to instantiate the views. Use registerXMLView() to add your own views to the table so that you can use them in your own XML files.

methods.name: createFromXMLElement
methods.doc: Creates a view from the given XML element (node and attributes). The method handleXMLElement() is executed for each child node in the XML. Uses the internal lookup table to instantiate the views. Use registerXMLView() to add your own views to the table so that you can use them in your own XML files.

methods.name: createFromXMLFile
methods.doc: Creates a view from the given XML file path. The method handleXMLElement() is executed for each child node in the XML. Uses the internal lookup table to instantiate the views. Use registerXMLView() to add your own views to the table so that you can use them in your own XML files.

methods.name: createFromXMLResource
methods.doc: Creates a view from the given XML resource file name. The method handleXMLElement() is executed for each child node in the XML. Uses the internal lookup table to instantiate the views. Use registerXMLView() to add your own views to the table so that you can use them in your own XML files.

methods.name: handleXMLElement
methods.doc: Handles a child XML element. You can redefine this method to handle child XML like as you want in your own views. If left unimplemented, will throw an exception because raw views cannot handle child XML elements (Boxes can).

methods.name: applyXMLAttributes
methods.doc: Applies the attributes of the given XML element to the view. You can add your own attributes to by calling registerXMLAttribute() in the view constructor.

methods.sig: virtual bool applyXMLAttribute(std::string name, std::string value)
methods.name: applyXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Applies the given attribute to the view. You can add your own attributes to by calling registerXMLAttribute() in the view constructor.

methods.name: registerAutoXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has the value "auto".

methods.name: registerPercentageXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has a percentage value (an integer with "%" suffix). The given float value is guaranteed to be between 0.0f and 1.0f.

methods.name: registerFloatXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has an integer, float, @style or "px" value.

methods.name: registerStringXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has a string or @i18n value. If you use string as a type, you can only have one handler for the attribute.

methods.name: registerColorXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has a color value ("#XXXXXX" or "#XXXXXXXX") or a @theme value.

methods.name: registerBoolXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has a boolean value ("true" or "false").

methods.name: registerFilePathXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Register a new XML attribute with the given name and handler method. You can have multiple attributes registered with the same name but different types / handlers, except if the type is string. The method will be called if the attribute has a file path value ("@res/" or raw path).

methods.name: getXMLCache
methods.doc: Get the XML document for the XML file, creating a new one if none is cached.

methods.name: isXMLAttributeValid
methods.doc: Returns if the given XML attribute name is valid for that view.

methods.name: setMaximumAllowedXMLElements
methods.doc: Sets the maximum number of allowed children XML elements when using a view of that class in an XML file.

methods.name: setInFadeAnimation
methods.doc: If set to true, will force the view to be translucent.

methods.name: setFocusable
methods.doc: Sets the view to be focusable. Required to be able to use actions that need focus on that view (such as an A press).

methods.name: removeFromSuperView
methods.doc: Removes view from it's parent

methods.name: setFocusSound
methods.doc: Sets the sound to play when this view gets focused.

methods.name: detach
methods.doc: Sets the detached flag to true. This action is irreversible. A detached view will, as the name suggests, not be attached to their parent Yoga node. That means that invalidation and layout need to be taken care of manually by the parent. detach() must be called before adding the view to the parent.

methods.name: setDetachedPosition
methods.doc: Sets the position of the view, if detached.

methods.name: setDetachedPositionX
methods.doc: Sets the position X of the view, if detached.

methods.name: setDetachedPositionY
methods.doc: Sets the position Y of the view, if detached.

methods.name: getDetachedPosition
methods.doc: Gets detached position of the view.

methods.sig: void setParent(Box* parent, void* parentUserdata = nullptr)
methods.name: setParent

methods.sig: ActionIdentifier registerAction(std::string hintText, enum ControllerButton button, ActionListener actionListener, bool hidden = false, bool allowRepeating = false, enum Sound sound = SOUND_NONE)
methods.name: registerAction
methods.doc: Registers an action with the given parameters. The listener will be fired when the user presses the key when the view is focused. The listener should return true if the action was consumed, false otherwise. The sound will only be played if the listener returned true. A hidden action will not show up in the bottom-right hints. Returns the identifier for the action, so it can be unregistered later on. Returns ACTION_NONE if the action was not registered.

methods.name: unregisterAction
methods.doc: Unregisters an action with the given identifier.

methods.name: registerClickAction
methods.doc: Shortcut to register a generic "A OK" click action.

methods.sig: void updateActionHint(enum ControllerButton button, std::string hintText)
methods.name: updateActionHint

methods.sig: void setActionAvailable(enum ControllerButton button, bool available)
methods.name: setActionAvailable

methods.sig: void playClickAnimation(bool reverse = false, bool animateBack = true, bool force = false)
methods.name: playClickAnimation
getGestureRecognizers
methods.doc: Get the vector of all gesture recognizers attached to that view.

methods.name: interruptGestures
methods.doc: Interrupt every recognizer on this view. If onlyIfUnsureState == true, only recognizers with current state UNSURE will be interupted

methods.name: addGestureRecognizer
methods.doc: Add new gesture recognizer on this view.

methods.sig: Sound gestureRecognizerRequest(TouchState touch, MouseState mouse, View* firstResponder)
methods.name: gestureRecognizerRequest
methods.doc: Called each frame when touch is registered. @returns sound to play invoked by touch recognizers.

methods.name: frame
methods.doc: Called each frame Do not override it to draw your view, override draw() instead

methods.name: frameHighlight
methods.doc: Called each frame

methods.sig: virtual void draw(NVGcontext* vg, float x, float y, float width, float height, Style style, FrameContext* ctx) = 0
methods.name: draw
methods.doc: Called by frame() to draw the view onscreen. Views should not draw outside of their bounds (they may be clipped if they do so).

methods.name: willAppear
methods.doc: Called when the view will appear on screen, before or after layout(). Can be called if the view has already appeared, so be careful.

methods.name: willDisappear
methods.doc: Called when the view will disappear from the screen. Can be called if the view has already disappeared, so be careful.

methods.name: onShowAnimationEnd
methods.doc: Called when the show() animation (fade in) ends

methods.name: show
methods.doc: Shows the view with a fade in animation.

methods.sig: virtual void show(std::function<void(void)> cb, bool animate, float animationDuration)
methods.name: show
methods.doc: Shows the view with a fade in animation, or no animation at all.

methods.name: getShowAnimationDuration
methods.doc: Returns the duration of the view show / hide animation.

methods.name: collapse
methods.doc: Hides the view in a collapse animation

methods.name: expand
methods.doc: Shows the view in a expand animation (opposite of collapse)

methods.name: hide
methods.doc: Hides the view with a fade out animation.

methods.sig: virtual void hide(std::function<void(void)> cb, bool animate, float animationDuration)
methods.name: hide
methods.doc: Hides the view with a fade out animation, or no animation at all.

methods.name: isTranslucent
methods.doc: Is this view translucent? If you override it please return <value> || View::isTranslucent() to keep the fadeIn transition

methods.name: getDefaultFocus
methods.doc: Returns the default view to focus when focusing this view Typically the view itself or one of its children. Returning nullptr means that the view is not focusable (and neither are its children) By default, a view is focusable if the flag is set to true with setFocusable() and if the view is visible. When pressing a key, the flow is :  1. starting from the currently focused view's parent, traverse the tree upwards and    repeatedly call getNextFocus() on every view until we find a next view to focus or meet the end of the tree  2. if a view is found, getNextFocus() will internally call getDefaultFocus() for the selected child  3. give focus to the result, if it exists

methods.name: hitTest
methods.doc: Returns the view to focus with the corresponding screen coordinates in the view or its children, or nullptr if it hasn't been found. Research is done recursively by traversing the tree starting from this view. This view's parents are not traversed.

methods.sig: virtual View* getNextFocus(FocusDirection direction, View* currentView)
methods.name: getNextFocus
methods.doc: Returns the next view to focus given the requested direction and the currently focused view (as parent user data) Returning nullptr means that there is no next view to focus in that direction - getNextFocus will then be called on our parent if any

methods.name: setCustomNavigationRoute
methods.doc: Sets a custom navigation route from this view to the target one.

methods.name: setCustomNavigationRoute
methods.doc: Sets a custom navigation route from this view to the target one, by ID. The final target view will be the "nearest" with the given ID. Resolution of the ID to View is made when the navigation event occurs, not when the route is registered.

methods.name: onFocusGained
methods.doc: Fired when focus is gained.

methods.name: onFocusLost
methods.doc: Fired when focus is lost.

methods.name: onParentFocusGained
methods.doc: Fired when focus is gained on this view's parent, or the parent of the parent...

methods.name: onParentFocusLost
methods.doc: Fired when focus is lost on one of this view's parents. Works similarly to onParentFocusGained().

methods.name: onWindowSizeChanged
methods.doc: Fired when the window size changes, after updating layout.

methods.sig: float getClickAlpha() { return this->clickAlpha; } /** * Forces this view and its children to use * the specified theme. */ void overrideTheme(Theme* newTheme)
methods.name: getClickAlpha
setCulled
methods.doc: Enables / disable culling for that view. To disable culling for all child views of a Box use setCullingEnabled on the box.

methods.sig: void setBackgroundCornerRadii(float topLeft, float topRight, float bottomRight, float bottomLeft)
methods.name: setBackgroundCornerRadii
methods.doc: Sets the background corner radii of the view. Only for vertical linear style.

methods.name: setTranslationY
methods.doc: Sets the Y translation of this view. Translation is applied after the layout phase. Use relative position and setPosition methods if possible instead.

methods.name: setTranslationX
methods.doc: Sets the X translation of this view. Translation is applied after the layout phase. Use relative position and setPosition methods if possible instead.

methods.name: setWireframeEnabled
methods.doc: Wireframe mode allows you to see the view size and margins (and padding if applicable) directly in your app. Useful to diagnose views misplacements or display bugs.

methods.name: getStringXMLAttributeValue
methods.doc: Resolves the value of the given XML attribute string. Applies i18n if the value is an "@i18n/" string, returns the string as it is otherwise.

methods.name: getFilePathXMLAttributeValue
methods.doc: Resolves the value of the given XML attribute file path. Returns the full path of the resource if it starts with "@res/", returns the path as it is otherwise.

methods.name: getParentNavigationDecision
addView
methods.doc: Adds a view to this Box. Returns the position the view was added at.

methods.sig: virtual void addView(View* view, size_t position)
methods.name: addView
methods.doc: Adds a view to this Box at the given position. Returns the position the view was added at.

methods.name: setPadding
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children. Only does one layout pass instead of four when using the four methods separately.

methods.sig: virtual void setPadding(float top, float right, float bottom, float left)
methods.name: setPadding
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children. Only does one layout pass instead of four when using the four methods separately.

methods.name: setPaddingTop
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children.

methods.name: setPaddingRight
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children.

methods.name: setPaddingBottom
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children.

methods.name: setPaddingLeft
methods.doc: Sets the padding of the view, aka the internal space to give between this view boundaries and its children.

methods.name: setJustifyContent
methods.doc: Sets the children alignment along the Box axis. Default is FLEX_START.

methods.name: setAlignItems
methods.doc: Sets the children alignment along the Box cross axis. Default is AUTO.

methods.name: setDirection
methods.doc: Sets the direction of the box, aka place the views left to right or right to left (flips the children). Default is INHERIT.

methods.sig: virtual void getCullingBounds(float* top, float* right, float* bottom, float* left)
methods.name: getCullingBounds

methods.name: forwardXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Registers an XML attribute to be forwarded to the given view. Works regardless of the target attribute type. Useful to expose attributes of children views in the parent box without copy pasting them individually. The forwarded attribute value will override the value of the regular attribute if it already exists in the target view.

methods.sig: void forwardXMLAttribute(std::string attributeName, View* target, std::string targetAttributeName)
methods.name: forwardXMLAttribute
methods.doc: Registers an XML attribute to be forwarded to the given view, while changing the target attribute name. Works regardless of the target attribute type. Useful to expose attributes of children views in the parent box without copy pasting them individually, but with a different name. The forwarded attribute value will override the value of the regular attribute if it already exists in the target view.

methods.sig: virtual void onChildFocusGained(View* directChild, View* focusedView)
methods.name: onChildFocusGained
methods.doc: Fired when focus is gained on one of this view's children, or one of the children of the children... directChild is guaranteed to be one of your children. It may not be the view that has been focused. If focusedView == directChild, then the child of yours has been focused. Otherwise, focusedView is a child of directChild.

methods.name: onChildFocusLost

Image.doc: An image. The view will try to grow as much as possible to fit the image. The scaling type dictates what to do with the image if there is not enough or too much space for the view compared to the image inside. Supported formats are: JPG, PNG, TGA, BMP and GIF (not animated).

setInterpolation
methods.doc: Sets the interpolation method for the image. Default is LINEAR. As the interpolation is set when the texture is created, and since we don't want to always store the image buffer in the view, this only takes effect after (re) loading the image using the setImage* methods. If you are using the interpolation XML attribute, you have to set it before the actual image attribute.

Label.name: Label
Label.doc: Some text. The Label will automatically grow as much as possible. If there is enough space, the label dimensions will fit the text. If there is not enough horizontal space available, it will wrap and expand its height. If there is not enough vertical space available to wrap, the text will be truncated instead. The truncated text will animate if the Label or one of its parents is focused. Animation will be disabled if the alignment is other than LEFT. Warning: to wrap, the label width MUST be constrained

methods.name: setHorizontalAlign
methods.doc: Sets the alignment of the text inside the view. Will not move the view, only the text inside. Default is CENTER.

methods.name: setVerticalAlign
methods.doc: Sets the alignment of the text inside the view. Will not move the view, only the text inside. Only applies to single-line labels. Default is CENTER.

methods.name: setAnimated
methods.doc: If an "animated" label is too large to fit its bounds, the full text will be displayed in a scrolling animation instead of being truncated with an ellipsis ("..."). Unless the autoAnimate flag is set to false, a label will automatically be set to "animated" if it is focused or if one of its parent is.

methods.name: setAutoAnimate
methods.doc: Controls whether focus changes automatically animates the label or not. Doesn't stop the ongoing animation should there be one.

methods.name: setSingleLine
methods.doc: A single-line label will not wrap and increase its height, even if the remaining vertical space allows it. Instead, it will always be truncated (if too large) to fit the horizontal space.
